identity.name: Western Turks after the Tang conquest (Cliopatria 'Turks')

land.text: Zhetysu and the Chu valley with Chach, which the Tang held after the fall of the Western Turkic Khaganate in 657-659 and which the Western Turks hold again, as Tang proxies, from 666

predecessors.note: The Tang annexed the Western Turks' lands in 657 (the tang-dynasty example, /ledger/11, gains Dzungaria and Semirechye from western-gokturks) and ruled them through two puppet qaghans, Mishe and Buzhen ('After the defeat of Ashina Helu in 657, the Tang emperor Gaozong installed two puppet qaghans', Western Turkic Khaganate page). Cliopatria's 'Turks' begins in 666, the year that page gives for Buzhen's death. western-gokturks (ia-01-d) ends in 657, hands its land to the Tang and names no turks successor, so it is not this state's predecessor in the ledger; the people are the same (the alt_names say so).

land.text: the Taraz core from which Wuzhile founded the Turgesh khaganate in 699 (infobox capitals Taraz and Suyab)

successors.note: 'The leadership of the Western Turks was taken up by the Turgesh' (Western Turkic Khaganate page, undated). The turgesh dossier founds on this core in 699 (/ledger/0, counterpart turks) and takes the rest of Semirechye, Dzungaria, Chach and Turfan from tang-dynasty in 703 (/ledger/1).

land.text: the rest of the Western Turks' land outside the Taraz core, nominally Tang until the Turgesh take it in 703

successors.note: 698-702: no Turkic state is drawn outside the Taraz core. Western Turkic Khaganate page: Suyab was a Tang Anxi garrison 679-719 and the attempts to install Ashina Huaidao as ruler of the Western Turks in 699 and 700 failed; the turgesh dossier gains this land from tang-dynasty in 703.

capitals.name: Suyab (Ak-Beshim)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: Navekat (summer) and Suyab (principal)' for the khaganate as a whole; the page does not say where the post-657 Turks sat. Ends in 678 because 'From 679 to 719 the old Göktürk capital of Suyab was one of the Four Garrisons of Anxi' (same page). No capital is given for 679-698: the page names no seat of the Western Turks in those years, and Navekat (the summer capital, not in the gazetteer) is the khaganate's, not shown for the remnant. The Protectorate General to Pacify the West page moves the Tang Anxi seat to Suyab after the 670 defeat at the Dafei River (undated), so even 670-678 is doubtful; coordinates are the gazetteer's Suyab.

correction.text: the Western Turk tribes' grazing lands of Zhetysu and the Ili side of Dzungaria with Chach, without Sogdia and the Ferghana valley (the page names the Chu valley seats Suyab and Navekat and the Duolu in the east and Nushibi in the west)

keyframe_review.note: 666-673, 0.70 M km2: Zhetysu (74 percent of it) with Sogdia (58 percent of Transoxiana), Ferghana (74 percent) and Chach. The Western Turkic Khaganate page names the Chu valley seats Suyab and Navekat and puts Duolu in the east and Nushibi in the west, and has the Tang rule the area through puppets ('Mishe was killed by Buzhen in 662', 'Buzhen was himself killed in 666'); it gives no Western Turk holding in Sogdia or Ferghana, so both are taken out (about 0.33 M km2 remains, Chach kept). No area on the page for these years (infobox 3.5 M km2 is for 630).

correction.text: the Western Turk tribes' grazing lands of Zhetysu and the Ili side of Dzungaria with Chach, without Sogdia and the Ferghana valley (the page names the Chu valley seats Suyab and Navekat and the Duolu in the east and Nushibi in the west)

keyframe_review.note: 674-691, 0.97 M km2: the 666 shape plus 750 cells of Dzungaria (37 percent of it), the Ili side where the Duolu lived. Same correction (about 0.56 M km2). The page: 'In 677, Duzhi declared himself Onoq Khagan, ruler of all Turks. He took Kucha with Tibetan help'; 'In 679 ... Tang forces recaptured the Four Garrisons'; 'captured by the Tibetan Empire between 686-689' (Yuanqing); 'Böri ... was defeated in 690 during an invasion by the Second Turkic Khaganate'. The Protectorate General to Pacify the West page: 'In 673 the Tang consolidated control over the Wuduolu Turks living in the area that came to be known as Dzungaria', so the 750 Dzungaria cells are Turk tribes under Tang overlordship, not nobody's land.

correction.text: the Western Turk tribes' grazing lands of Zhetysu and the Ili side of Dzungaria with Chach, without Sogdia and the Ferghana valley (the page names the Chu valley seats Suyab and Navekat and the Duolu in the east and Nushibi in the west)

keyframe_review.note: 692-717, 0.96 M km2. Years only 692-698: the same corrected shape. From 699 the Türgesh page has Wuzhile found the Turgesh khaganate, and the Cliopatria 'Türgesh' shape of 705-717 contains this one, so 699-717 belongs to the turgesh dossier. At 698 only the Taraz core (150 km) passes to the Turgesh (turgesh /ledger/0); the rest of the shape goes to the Tang in the ledger (loss, confidence 1) and comes to the Turgesh in 703 (turgesh /ledger/1, gain from tang-dynasty).

correction.text: years only: no 'Turks' state in 750-756; the land is the Tang Anxi protectorate, the Turgesh remnant in Zhetysu (to 766) and Karluk country

keyframe_review.note: 750, 0.78 M km2: the whole Pamir, Ferghana (91 percent of it), Chach, Transoxiana (63 percent) and Zhetysu (52 percent). No page opened names a Turkic state with this shape in 750: the Western Turkic Khaganate page has Tang control of the area 'until the time of An Lushan's rebellion in 756', the Karluks page has the Karluks 'split from the Tang' in 751 and the Arabs push them out of Ferghana, the Türgesh page has the Turgesh in Zhetysu to 766. The area is Tang protectorate, Turgesh and Karluk country, not a 'Turks' polity; Cliopatria's Tang and Uyghur shapes also overlap it.

correction.text: years only: no 'Turks' state in 750-756; Talas (751) moves Transoxiana from Tang influence to the Abbasids

keyframe_review.note: 751-754, 0.64 M km2: the same lands after the Battle of Talas (July 751): 'the Tang lost influence there and Abbasid forces re-established control over Transoxiana' (757-775 per the page). Not a Turkic state; see turks_750.

correction.text: years only: the Pamir-Karakoram marches of 755-756 are not a 'Turks' state

keyframe_review.note: 755-756, 0.16 M km2 (547 cells: 236 on the western edge of the Tarim Basin, 180 in the Pamir, 63 in Gilgit-Baltistan, the rest in Afghanistan): the marches where the page has Gao Xianzhi secure Gilgit in 747 and the Tang withdraw from Anxi after An Lushan's rebellion in 755. No page opened gives a Turk there.

region.text: Zhetysu and the Chu valley with Chach

ledger.note: 666: Buzhen, the last Tang-appointed ruler of the Western Turks' Nushibi, is killed and the Turks continue under Ashina claimants. 'Mishe was killed by Buzhen in 662, and Buzhen was killed in 666' (Western Turkic Khaganate page; its infobox gives Buzhen '657–667'). The Ashina Buzhen page gives 'Reign: 657–667' and 'Died: 667', does not say he was killed, and has 'When Buzhen died in 667, Tang influence in the region was greatly reduced'; the pages differ by a year, and 666 is kept as the first page's text and Cliopatria's first year. Neither page calls this a founding (confidence 1). The land was the Tang's since 657 (tang-dynasty example /ledger/11, gain from western-gokturks, which ends in 657), so the counterpart is the Tang, not western-gokturks. The land is the Chu valley seats and Zhetysu.

region.text: Zhetysu and the Chu valley with Chach, the Nushibi and Duolu tribes under the Tang puppet qaghans

ledger.note: 666: the Western Turks are the Tang's vassal. Infobox: 'Vassal of the Tang dynasty (657–742)', with the 'Kunling Protectorate (657–736)' and 'Mengchi Protectorate (657–742)'; Gaozong 'installed two puppet qaghans', Mishe over the five Duolu tribes in the east and Buzhen over the five Nushibi in the west. The relation begins in 657-659, before this state's first year, so the year is the state's start (confidence 2); the page does not say which tribes either protectorate covered. Mirror: tang-dynasty (ea-04) should carry the vassal_start and vassal_end with counterpart turks for 666-677 and 685-690.

region.text: Dzungaria on the Ili side, the Duolu country east of the Chu

ledger.note: 674: the Ili side of Dzungaria, where the Duolu lived, is drawn as Turk land. Cliopatria adds 750 cells of Dzungaria in 674. Protectorate General to Pacify the West page: 'In 673 the Tang consolidated control over the Wuduolu Turks living in the area that came to be known as Dzungaria'; Western Turkic Khaganate page: the Tang assigned Duzhi 'the Wuduolu Turks' by 671. So the land was the Tang's, not nobody's, and the Turks hold it only as Tang proxies (the vassal_start below). The year is Cliopatria's, a year after the page's 673 (confidence 1, bridging).

region.text: the Duolu country in Dzungaria, east of the Chu

ledger.note: 674: the Dzungaria piece enters the same Tang overlordship as the Chu and Zhetysu lands ('In 673 the Tang consolidated control over the Wuduolu Turks', Protectorate General to Pacify the West page); the year is Cliopatria's 674 against the page's 673.

region.text: Zhetysu and the Chu valley with Chach

ledger.note: 677: 'In 677, Duzhi declared himself Onoq Khagan, ruler of all Turks' against the Tang, allied with Tibet (infobox: Duzhi '676–679 (allied with Tibetan Empire)'). The year is the page's; that the declaration ends the Tang overlordship is my reading. The Tang recover the Four Garrisons and capture Duzhi in 679.

region.text: the Duolu country in Dzungaria, east of the Chu

ledger.note: 677: Duzhi's own tribes are the Wuduolu Turks of Dzungaria ('The Tang had assigned Duzhi control of the Wuduolu Turks'), so the Dzungaria piece leaves the Tang overlordship with his declaration. Same page and reading as the entry above.

region.text: Kucha on the northern rim of the Tarim, one of the Four Garrisons

ledger.note: 677: Ashina Duzhi declares himself Onoq Khagan and takes Kucha with Tibetan help. 'In 677, Duzhi declared himself Onoq Khagan, ruler of all Turks. He took Kucha with Tibetan help.' The page gives the year for the declaration; the Kucha capture is in the same sentence. The Protectorate General to Pacify the West page instead gives the capture of Qiuci (Kucha) in 677 to the Tibetan Empire alone ('In 677 the Tibetan Empire captured Qiuci'), and the tang-dynasty example books the 679 recovery as a gain from tibetan-empire (/ledger/20): the pages disagree on who held Kucha in 677-679, and the Tang side of the ledger may name Tibet where this one names the Turks.

region.text: Kucha on the northern rim of the Tarim, one of the Four Garrisons

ledger.note: 679: Pei Xingjian recovers the Four Garrisons and captures Duzhi. 'In 679 Tang envoys traveled to Tibet for negotiations' while Tang forces recaptured the Four Garrisons; Pei Xingjian 'lured Duzhi and his leaders into capture'.

region.text: the Western Turks' grazing lands of Zhetysu and the Ili side of Dzungaria with Chach

ledger.note: 685: 'Empress Wu Zetian sent Yuanqing and Böri westward in 685 to succeed their fathers as proxy rulers' (Yuanqing the son of Mishe, Böri of Buzhen; both had 'resided in Chang'an'). The year is the page's; the extent is my reading (the whole corrected shape). The Tang hold is nominal: Yuanqing 'was captured by the Tibetan Empire between 686-689' and 'Turkic tribes resisted' him.

region.text: the Western Turks' grazing lands of Zhetysu and the Ili side of Dzungaria with Chach

ledger.note: 690: Böri 'was able to bring the western tribes temporarily under his rule, but was defeated in 690 during an invasion by the' Second Turkic Khaganate and fled to the Tang (executed 692). The page names no other Tang-appointed ruler of the Western Turks until the failed installation of Huaidao in 699 and 700, so the proxy rule is ended here rather than at the infobox's 742. The Second Turkic Khaganate page, opened again, does not mention the 690 invasion.

region.text: Zhetysu, the Chu valley, Chach and the Ili side of Dzungaria outside the Taraz core

ledger.note: 698: the Western Turks' land outside the Taraz core is no one's Turkic state until the Turgesh take it in 703. Western Turkic Khaganate page: Suyab was a Tang Anxi garrison 679-719 and 'Efforts were made to install Böri's son, Ashina Huaidao, as ruler of the Western Turks in 699 and 700' (failed); the Türgesh page (turgesh /ledger/1) has Wuzhile take 'the territory from Chach to Turfan and Beshbaliq' from the Tang in 703. The page dates none of this to 698: confidence 1, drawn so that this dossier and turgesh agree.

region.text: the Taraz core from which the Turgesh khaganate was founded

ledger.note: 698: the Western Turk remnant gives way to the Turgesh. Türgesh page: Wuzhile 'established a khaganate in 699', with Taraz and Suyab as capitals; the Western Turkic Khaganate page: 'the leadership of the Western Turks was taken up by the Turgesh'. turgesh /ledger/0 founds on a 150 km Taraz core with counterpart turks, so only that core passes to the Turgesh here; the rest is the loss to the Tang above. The page gives no end year: 698 is drawn so that the two dossiers meet.

wars.name: Duzhi's revolt and the Tang recovery of the Four Garrisons

zones.text: Kucha and the Four Garrisons of the Tarim

wars.outcome: Duzhi takes Kucha with Tibetan help (677); Pei Xingjian recovers the garrisons and captures him (679).
wars.note: Duzhi was a Tang appointee in 671 ('The Tang had assigned Duzhi control of the Wuduolu Turks').

wars.name: Tibetan capture of Ashina Yuanqing
wars.outcome: Yuanqing, sent west by Wu Zetian in 685, is captured by Tibet between 686 and 689. No territory is named.
wars.note: Zones left empty: the Western Turkic Khaganate page gives no ground for the capture. The Protectorate General to Pacify the West page, opened again, has 'In 687 the Tibetan Empire established control over the Western Regions' and 'In 690 the Tibetan Empire defeated a Tang army at Issyk-Kul' but does not mention the Turks, so no zone is drawn from it.

wars.name: Second Turkic invasion of the Western Turks
wars.outcome: Böri (Ashina Huseluo) is defeated in 690 by the Second Turkic Khaganate and flees to the Tang with his followers; he is executed in 692. No territory is named.
wars.note: Zones left empty: the Second Turkic Khaganate page, opened again, has no sentence on this invasion or on Böri; its only statement on the western limit in these years is that 'between 698 and 701 the northern and western frontiers of Qapaghan's state were defined by the Tannu Ola, Altai and Tarbagatai mountain ranges', which would put the 690 raid no further than the Tarbagatai, east of the Ili country (my reading, not drawn).

certainty.note: Tribal grazing lands under Tang, Tibetan and Turkic pressure; no line is given by any page.

notes: What the row is: Cliopatria's 'Turks' (666-756) has Wikipedia title 'Turk' (a disambiguation page, nothing on a medieval state) and Wikidata Q2118293, which the table shares with 'Oghuz Turks'. The shapes are Zhetysu with Sogdia, Ferghana and Chach (666-717) and then Pamir, Ferghana, Transoxiana and Zhetysu (750-754) and a Pamir-Karakoram remnant (755-756). The two rows are different states: the Oghuz Yabgu State lies on the Aral and lower Syr Darya, the Turks row on the Chu and Ili. Resolution (label swap, partly confirmed): the brief's guess that 'Türgesh' (Mongolia) and 'Turks' (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan) were swapped fits the shapes only in part. 'Türgesh' 692-704 is the Second Turkic Khaganate; 'Türgesh' 705-749 is that plus the real Turgesh lands, so the real Turgesh are covered by the turgesh dossier (699-766). 'Turks' 692-717 lies wholly inside the 705-717 Türgesh shape, so it is not a second state in those years. What the pages support as a distinct 'Turks' state is only the Western Turk remnant under Tang puppets, Ashina claimants (Duzhi 671-679, Yuanqing and Böri 685-692) and Tibetan pressure, 666-698; that is what this dossier keeps, soft and thin (twelve ledger events after the repair of 2026-10-19, three wars; the page gives no border and no area). Dropped: Sogdia and Ferghana (no page gives the Western Turks a holding there after 657; the Muslim conquest of Transoxiana page shows local kings under Turgesh overlords from 719), and the 750-756 shapes (no Turks state: Tang protectorate until 756, Karluks from 751, Turgesh in Zhetysu to 766). Open points: the Tang dossier should carry Tang suzerainty over the Western Turks, with this state as counterpart, for 666-677 and 685-690 (see below); the Western Turk-Tibetan alliance of 677; the Second Turkic invasion of 690 does not say where it fell. Names the gazetteer lacks: Navekat (summer capital, Chu valley). Repair of 2026-10-19 (reviewer verdict fail): (1) the 666 found takes its land from tang-dynasty, not western-gokturks (which ends in 657 and hands its land to the Tang); tang-dynasty replaces western-gokturks in predecessors. (2) Tang suzerainty is now in the ledger: vassal_start 666 (Semirechye and Chach) and 674 (the Duolu country of Dzungaria), both ended 677 by Duzhi's declaration; a second vassal_start 685 (Yuanqing and Böri as proxies) ended 690 (Böri's defeat). Following the convention of the fixed dossiers (umma.json), the counterpart is the suzerain in this state's own ledger, as the mirror of the vassal_start tang-dynasty should carry with counterpart turks. (3) The 698 hand-over now agrees with turgesh: only the Taraz core (150 km) goes to the Turgesh (turgesh /ledger/0), the rest is a loss to the Tang at 698 (confidence 1) and comes to the Turgesh in 703 (turgesh /ledger/1, from tang-dynasty). (4) The Suyab capital ends in 678 (Suyab a Tang garrison 679-719); no capital is drawn for 679-698. The 679-698 shape still contains the Suyab garrison: the page gives it no extent, and the Protectorate and Tang-example pages date and attribute it differently, so it is left to ea-04. (5) The 674 Dzungaria gain names tang-dynasty (Protectorate page: Tang control of the Wuduolu Turks in 673). (6) wikidata is left null: Q2118293 is Cliopatria's id and is shared with Oghuz Turks; wikidata.org is unreachable and the Wikipedia page-information route failed, so the Western Turkic Khaganate's own item could not be read; polities.csv keeps Cliopatria's value. Disagreements kept: Buzhen's death year (Western Turkic Khaganate page 666, Ashina Buzhen page 667; 666 kept); who held Kucha in 677-679 (Western Turkic Khaganate page: Duzhi with Tibet; Protectorate page and the Tang example: Tibet); Suyab (Anxi seat after 670 on the Protectorate page, the khaganate's capital on the infobox).
